Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + reference request for Solstice — claims automation use case

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really excited by Solstice's roadmap for modernizing claims processing. As we discussed, the procurement and security teams want to speak with a couple of Redwood customers who have run similar large-scale claims automation workloads in the last 12 months (particularly multi-tenant ingestion, PII handling, and sub-second routing for triage).

Would you be open to a short, 30-minute reference call? If it helps speed things along I can curate a two-pack of advocates that are close matches by both industry (insurance) and use case (claims triage/automation) and share the scope and suggested agenda up front. We can also keep any call on the record or off-the-record per your preference.

Proposed next steps from my side: assemble two advocates, share one-pager of topics (data residency, model performance, integration pattern), and propose two 30-min windows next week. If you prefer to scope a narrower ask for procurement (e.g., just security posture and SOC2 artifacts) say the word and I’ll tailor.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Ben —

Thanks for following up. Procurement/InfoSec are specifically interested in examples where Redwood handled:
- Tenant isolation for multiple carriers
- PII redaction and audit logging
- Predictable latency for routing/triage pipelines

We prefer references who can speak to production stability and operational support (on-call, runbook handover). Also a US-based example would be ideal because of our regulatory constraints.

We’re happy with a short call. Ideally the advocate can speak to concrete build/ops tradeoffs rather than marketing high-level outcomes. Two advocates is perfect.

Could you also indicate whether the advocates are comfortable signing a short NDA / discussing a scaled MOU? Procurement requires.

Best,
Elena Morales
VP, Claims Transformation
Solstice Insurance
